title: Asia Markets & Central Banks (Korea Rate-Hike Bets, RBI Rupee Moves, SK Hynix Slide, India IPO Boom)
summary: Gotrade News - SK Hynix (SKHY) fell 2.97% in early Seoul trading on Monday, October 12, dragging the Kospi lower, as traders braced for more Bank of Korea
body_markdown:
## Will the Bank of Korea Raise Rates Again?


As reported by[The Edge Malaysia](https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/819600) , South Korea's three-year bond yield jumped 11 basis points to 4.11% on September 28 when markets reopened after a holiday, the highest level since November 2022.


The Bank of Korea has already delivered back-to-back rate hikes and is expected to likely raise rates again in November if the Federal Reserve hikes in October, the report said.


The selloff followed a global bond rout driven by elevated oil prices tied to the Middle East conflict, with US Treasury yields climbing to their highest level in more than two decades during the Asian holiday closure. Kang Seungwon of NH Investment and Securities summed up the mood:


> "Korean yields surging shows this isn't just a US issue, and the market grows concerned the Bank of Korea will deliver more hikes."


## How Far Is the Rupee From Its Record Low?


Per[Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/rupee-near-record-low-why-rbis-multiple-defences-are-losing-effectiveness-560381-2026-10-08) , the rupee traded around 96.68 to 97 per dollar on October 8, close to its record low of 96.97 set in May 2026, after losing more than 7% this year.


The Reserve Bank of India has sold dollars in the spot market, used sell/buy swaps in the forward market, and delivered its first rate hike in nearly four years.


Those defenses have come at a cost: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $51 billion in four weeks, from a $785 billion peak to $734 billion as of October 2, according to Business Today.


The report cited elevated crude prices, rising global bond yields and about $30 billion of foreign selling in Indian equities in 2026, while RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the currency "may be undervalued."


## How Big Is India's 2026 IPO Boom?


Indian companies raised a record $12.5 billion through[initial public offerings](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) from January to September, the highest for the period since records began in 1980, according to LSEG data reported by[Telangana Today](https://telanganatoday.com/ipos-in-india-hit-record-12-5-billion-in-jan-sep-report) .


Domestic liquidity supported the market even as foreign portfolio investors sold Indian equities. The LSEG figures, as reported by Telangana Today, compare as follows:

September alone saw 34 mainboard IPOs raise Rs 39,380 crore, per the same report, though the average listing premium cooled to 15.1% from 24.4% in August.
